subject: Semantic index health check & model recommendations — SearchLytics pilot
body:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@searchlytics.com>; Tom Reynolds <treynolds@searchlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SearchLytics pilot — post-call notes & next steps

Hi Lena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Goal: surface more relevant results for long-tail product queries on SearchLytics.com (64M docs, mixed HTML + PDF).
- Primary metric you care about: Recall@10 and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) for user queries across cold vs. warmed shards.
- Constraints: must keep per-query P95 latency <= 120ms (US region) and monthly embedding cost under your current threshold.

What I’m attaching: a small sample of encoded vectors we pulled during the call (searchlytics_encoding_samples.csv), your canonical prompt set (promptset_search_queries_v1.jsonl), and an initial metrics dump (semantic_metrics_report_q2.pdf).

Immediate next steps I’ll take:
1) Run a short embedding-fit test (1k queries, 10k doc subset) with 3 candidate models and share the bench results: a) text-embedding-3-large (2048d), b) open-similarity-small (1024d quantized), c) sbert-mini-transfer (384d).
2) Produce a small prompt/augmentation checklist for query-side preprocessing (punctuation, stop-word handling, query expansion for multi-term queries).
3) Draft a mutual action plan for a 2-week pilot harness (we’ll own the eval run; you’ll provision a sample export).

Can you confirm the sample export location and whether we should include older archived PDFs (you mentioned retention for 3 years)?

Thanks —
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: (searchlytics_encoding_samples.csv, promptset_search_queries_v1.jsonl, semantic_metrics_report_q2.pdf)

From: Lena Park <lena.park@searchlytics.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@searchlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SearchLytics pilot — post-call notes & next steps

Thanks Grace — that looks right. A couple quick clarifications:

- Include archived PDFs (3-year retention) in the 10k doc subset — they are often the hardest to match.
- Sample export will be at gs://searchlytics-pilot/exports/SL-9821/seed_1 (I'll share IAM this afternoon).

Can you also run an early check for vector dimensionality impact? Our current stack expects 1536 dims and switching dims affects storage and downstream ANN indexing.

— Lena
Principal Data Scientist, SearchLytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Lena Park <lena.park@searchlytics.com>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@searchlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SearchLytics pilot — post-call notes & next steps

Lena —

Quick model/metric snapshot after the sandboxed 1k x 10k run (summary here, full CSV attached in the Drive link):

- text-embedding-3-large (2048d): Recall@10 = 0.81, MRR = 0.62, median cosine_sim positive hits = 0.78. Latency (P95) = 110ms (non-quantized). Storage per vector ~= 16KB (float32).
- open-similarity-small (1024d, 8-bit quantized): Recall@10 = 0.73, MRR = 0.54, median cosine_sim = 0.72. Latency (P95) = 70ms. Storage per vector ~= 5KB (quantized).
- sbert-mini-transfer (384d): Recall@10 = 0.66, MRR = 0.48, median cosine_sim = 0.68. Latency (P95) = 40ms; storage ~= 1.6KB.

Observations: 1) Dimensionality has a straight tradeoff: large dims (2048) give better recall/MRR but drive index size and IO; 2) Quantized 1024d is a good middle-ground for your latency target while offering decent recall; 3) 384d swims on easily but loses edge-case long-tail recall.

Immediate recommendation: run the 2-week pilot using open-similarity-small (1024d 8-bit quant) on a warmed index, and run a controlled A/B against a text-embedding-3-large baseline for top K results. If storage budget permits, keep a hybrid index where we store high-dim vectors for recently-accessed docs and quantized vectors for older archives.

Known risk: drift for archived PDFs — OCR variability causes embedding drift versus HTML text. We should surface QC alerts when cosine distributions shift by >0.08 on a rolling 30-day window.

I'll prepare a short evaluation harness that produces Recall@k, MRR, cosine distribution plots, and a drift-alarm stub. See early results: https://redwood-inference.internal/evals/SL-9821-embedding-run

— Karthik
Sr. Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@searchlytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@searchlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 12:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SearchLytics pilot — post-call notes & next steps

Thanks Karthik — a few follow-ups: 
1) If we pick quantized 1024d, what are the migration steps for our ANN index (we currently use FAISS IVF-PQ with 1536d)?
2) How confident are you that quantization won’t mask semantic drift signals (i.e., small cosine shifts)?

Tom
Engineering Lead, SearchLytics

---

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@searchlytics.com>, Lena Park <lena.park@searchlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SearchLytics pilot — post-call notes & next steps

Tom —

Short answers: 1) Migration plan: we’d provide a small script to convert your FAISS index (re-encode vectors to 1024d + PQ params) and a rolling backfill process that keeps old 1536d vectors in a read-only bucket for fallback. We’ll coordinate with your infra team for a maintenance window (estimated 2–3 hours for the 10k subset).
2) On drift sensitivity: quantization does reduce the absolute cosine variance, but relative shifts remain detectable. Karthik will instrument the eval harness to run both quantized and float comparisons on a 1k query shadow set weekly so we can detect masking. We’ll flag if detection power drops beneath 80% for known regressions.

Next steps from our side (action owners in-line):
- Grace: share pilot MOP and schedule (EOD Thu) — DONE (see Drive).
- Karthik: deliver harness + run (ETA Fri) — in progress (I’ll upload results).
- Ben: prepare a cost/perf note on expected monthly embedding costs for 1024d vs 2048d (ETA Mon).
- Lena: confirm IAM path and whether SSO is required for the Drive links.

Ben (cc’d) — any immediate comments on cost tradeoffs you want to surface to SearchLytics?

Thanks all.
Grace
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Lena Park <lena.park@searchlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SearchLytics pilot — post-call notes & next steps

Quick cost note for visibility: 
- 2048d float (baseline): ~ $0.045 / k vectors stored per month (storage + index IO), expected monthly embedding compute cost ~ $1,200 for your projected volume at 1M queries/month.
- 1024d quantized (recommended pilot): ~ $0.015 / k vectors stored per month, compute cost ~ $620 / month; we estimate ~30% throughput improvement due to smaller memory footprint on your current FAISS config.
- 384d mini: lowest cost but degrades recall on tail queries by ~18% in our runs.

Recommendation: pilot with 1024d quantized; if A/B shows >6% lift in user-level conversion for the query cohorts, consider scoped backfill of recent month with 2048d for hot docs only.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
